thread:
alice_support: Heads-up — customer on eu-west-1 is seeing p99/API latency jump ~1.2s for generate requests. They say responses show the request was handled from ap-south-1. Sharing a quick traceroute + curl output we captured. Can infra/ingress take a look?

cheng_ingress: Which trace id and client IP? Are they setting any region preference headers or sticky cookies? Also: any recent routing rollouts? :thinking: 

alice_support: Trace id: 1f8b3c. Client region confirmed eu-west-1. No explicit prefer-region header from customer. Traceroute from their app host (sanitized):
```
traceroute to api.redwood.inference (13.52.1.2), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  1.1 ms
 2  52.95.23.11  23.3 ms  ap-gw
 3  13.52.1.2  430.7 ms  ap-south-1-host
```
And curl -v against our endpoint: 
```
$ curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" \"https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate\" -d '{"input":"hi"}'
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.inference
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< X-Served-Region: ap-south-1
< X-Request-ID: 1f8b3c
< Content-Type: application/json
< 
{...}
```
So request left eu-west edge and hit ap-south-1. Not sure why. 

dana_sre: Thanks. Two quick hypotheses: (1) healthcheck/rollout made eu-west pool transiently unhealthy -> smart routing fallback to ap-south for that customer, or (2) sticky session mapping expired and customer backend IP got mapped via a route that prefers lower-cost path. Will check routing logs for 1f8b3c. Can you repro with a header to force region and paste full request metadata?

ben_runtime: We had a canary earlier today that changed the health-check timeout from 1s -> 500ms for model-serving instances (PR #2456). If an instance is slow on cold start it may be marked unhealthy faster, triggering fallback routing. I'm looking at rollout window around 2026-03-16T10:23Z. deploy-bot: canary 2026-03-16T10:23 rolled to 20% in eu-west-1.

cheng_ingress: Repro steps I used locally (please run from customer-like host):
```bash
# simulate client from eu-west1
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" -H \"X-Client-Id: acme-corp\" -H \"Prefer-Region: eu-west-1\" https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate -d '{"input":"latency test"}'
```
If it still hits ap-south-1 we can query routing decisions by request id.

alice_support: Ran that from a client VM in eu-west. Still got ap-south-1 back: X-Served-Region ap-south-1, X-Request-ID 1f8b3c-repro. Repro steps recorded.

dana_sre: Ok. I'm pulling the routing decision log now. Quick grep result: 
```
routing.decisions | request_id=1f8b3c-repro | matched_policy=fallback-on-latency | chosen_region=ap-south-1 | reason=eu-west-1_pool_unhealthy_percent=67
```
Looks like eu-west pool was above unhealthy threshold at that moment and fallback policy chose ap-south. Need to know why the pool went unhealthy — could be the canary healthcheck change.

ben_runtime: Agreed. The PR lowered healthy threshold window and a batch of cold-starting model instances in eu-west failed one probe during the canary -> health ratio spiked briefly. I'm recommending rollback of that probe change and re-evaluation. I'll open an emergency PR to revert.

cheng_ingress: Meanwhile, we should make routing decisions include a region-affinity header for existing client sessions so they don't abruptly move cross-region on a single probe failure. Opening ticket to add session-grace (5 minutes) around failover.

alice_support: Thanks — I'll tell customer we've got a suspected canary + healthcheck interaction causing temporary eu->ap failover and that eng is rolling back. Will follow-up with ETA. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: [automated] canary rollback PR #2462 opened by ben_runtime at 2026-03-16T11:02:12Z

dana_sre: After rollback we should monitor same trace id window and confirm p99 returns to normal. I'll post follow-up logs once we see healthy counts back > 95%.

alice_support: Great. I'll mark the support ticket with these notes and ping if customer reports more spikes. Thanks everyone.
